Agung a tamlang 見於菲律賓，屬體鳴裂縫鼓，以掏空竹子模仿真實 a: The agung a tamlang is found in the Philippines and is an idiophone of the slit-drum type, made from hollowed bamboo in imitation of the real agung. Its development is bound up with the need to practise: because the pitch is set by the length and depth of the slit, it can stand in for a real agung as a practice instrument. Two common ways of playing have grown up: with one instrument, one hand holds it while the other strikes it with a beater; with two, the second is held by the foot.
Agung a tamlang的聆聽場合主要來自練習真正agung的音樂情境。來: The occasions for hearing the agung a tamlang come mainly from the musical situations in which a real agung is practised. The source names no particular composer, piece or kind of public performance, so the example should focus on its use as a practice instrument: the player may hold one in one hand and strike it with a beater in the other, or use two, one held by the foot and the other struck by hand. Its pitch is set by the length and depth of the slit in the bamboo, so the point in listening is the way it imitates the rhythm and pitch layout of the agung.
Agung a tamlang的音高由竹身裂縫的長度與深度決定，發聲來自掏空竹材: The pitch of the agung a tamlang is set by the length and depth of the slit in the bamboo, and it sounds as an idiophone: a slit drum made of hollowed bamboo. It imitates the real agung and serves as a practice instrument, so it differs from the real agung it imitates; it is struck with a beater, either one held in the hand or with another held by the foot.
agung a tamlang 是菲律賓的裂縫鼓，以掏空竹子製成，模仿真實的 a: The agung a tamlang is a Filipino slit drum made from hollowed bamboo in imitation of the real agung. Its pitch is set by the length and depth of the slit, and in the Hornbostel–Sachs classification it is 111.243, an idiophone. The player may hold one in one hand and strike it with a beater in the other, or use two at once with one held by the foot. It serves as a practice stand-in for the real agung, used by learners when they practise.
初學可先以單件練習：一手握持 Agung a tamlang，另一手持敲棒敲擊；: A beginner can start with a single instrument: hold the agung a tamlang in one hand and strike it with a beater in the other; with two, grip one of them between the feet. It sounds by striking the bamboo, and the pitch is set by the length and depth of the slit. As a practice instrument for the real agung, the point for a beginner is to master the hold, the stroke, and the one- or two-instrument grip.
